observation.visible_scene: A clear cylindrical glass stands on a white surface against a teal wall. Inside the glass are two unmixed liquid layers: a golden-yellow band floating above a transparent layer, with a pale white sediment settled at the bottom. A yellow drinking straw is inserted through the liquids, its upper end protruding above the rim. The glass, its liquid layers, and the sediment remain in place throughout the excerpt.
visible_changes: The yellow straw's apparent orientation relative to the glass changes across the segment: it goes from nearly vertical to increasingly slanted, with its top end shifting toward the right side of the rim while its lower end drifts leftward within the glass, consistent with the straw being tilted/rotated (or with a changing viewpoint).

The entire glass and its contents drift progressively leftward within the frame, and the soft vertical shadow/edge on the left of the background shifts, indicating camera movement (a pan) rather than the glass sliding on the surface.
The golden-yellow band and the clear layer keep a constant vertical position and thickness inside the glass; the white sediment at the bottom stays undisturbed.
Small bubbles/droplets clinging to the straw within the yellow band appear and shift slightly frame to frame.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the straw is being held and tilted by an unseen person, or whether its changing angle is purely a viewpoint/parallax effect.
The cause of the leftward drift of the glass in frame (camera pan vs. object motion) and what happens before the first and after the last sampled frame.
uncertain_details: Cannot definitively separate physical rotation of the straw from camera parallax, since the background is a featureless wall.
Cannot confirm whether the glass itself moves on the surface or only appears to shift due to camera translation.
The exact nature/identity of the two liquids and the sediment is not visually determinable from the clip.
